selectedText:
Senecio arenarius — Requested taxon account; preserve geographic and use qualifications.

Introduction: This bright, hardy annual will  grow well in large parts of South Africa.

Description: This is an annual herb up to 150–400 mm high. The glandular-hairy leaves are more or less clasping at the base, approximately 70 mm long and lobed into broad segments.

Distribution description: This species is found on sandy flats from the southern parts of Namibia and the Northern and Western Cape Provinces of South Africa, towards the Agulhas Plain. In both these provinces it grows both along the coast and further inland amongst, or as part of, seashore vegetation, fynbos (renosterveld and strandveld) and succulent karoo.

Distribution description: This species, given its vast geographical distribution, is subjected to various different climatic conditions. In some places the rainfall is about three times as much as others, and in the interior it experiences frost as opposed to none along the coast.

Ecology: It is likely that bees or beetles play a role in pollinating this species.

Use: No medicinal or cultural aspects have been recorded.

Use: Despite being an excellent annual with amazing horticultural potential, it is hardly found in cultivation.
